u-modena.note: The University dates Pillius's arrival from Bologna to 1175; Rashdall says only that it was before 1182. Continuity between the medieval studium and the 1682 foundation is disputed.

u-naples.note: Rashdall dates Conrad IV's attempt to move the studium to Salerno to 1253; how far it was carried out is unclear.

u-siena.note: Earliest notice of the studium is dated 1240 by the University and 1241 by older reference works.

u-rome-curia.note: The curia was itinerant in central Italy after 1251 (Perugia, Viterbo, Orvieto, Anagni); 'Rome' stands for that phase. The Studium Curiae appears to have been suppressed in favour of the city university only under Leo X (1513–21).

u-camerino.note: Early records were lost when the city archives were destroyed in 1259.

u-turin.note: The university was closed after the French occupation of 1536 and reopened at Mondovì before returning to Turin in 1566.

fix.summary: Advanced institute created by the Tuscan provisional government, with sections of letters/philosophy, medicine and natural sciences. It awarded degrees and became the University of Florence in 1923–24.

m-salerno-950-founding.note: Origins are traditionally placed between the 9th and 10th centuries; Treccani dates its flourishing from the mid-11th century.

u-bologna-1088-founding.note: 1088 is the conventional date; Irnerius is placed c. 1100–1130.

u-modena-1182-founding.note: Rashdall: Pillius left Bologna for Modena some time before 1182.

fix.desc: Masters and students leaving Bologna begin teaching in Vicenza.

u-vicenza-1204-founding.note: The 1204 migration is well attested; the sources do not connect it with Pillius, who was a civil lawyer.

u-siena-1240-founding.note: Older reference works give 1241 for the first notice.

u-rome-curia-1245-founding.note: Rashdall dates the foundation to 1244 or 1245.

u-naples-1252-relocation.note: Rashdall dates Conrad IV's attempt to move the studium to Salerno to 1253.

m-salerno-1280-charter.note: Charles of Anjou granted the school its first statute.

u-bologna-1291-charter.note: The Catholic Encyclopedia dates Nicholas IV's grant to 1292; 1291 is the date usually given.

u-camerino-1336-founding.note: The University places law teaching from the early 13th century; 1336 is the date of a papal nuncio's grant to the commune, not the start of teaching.

fix.desc: Innocent VI authorises a theological faculty, completing the university's full complement of faculties.

u-bologna-1364-charter.note: The theology faculty dates from 1360; Cardinal Albornoz's Collegio di Spagna followed in 1364.

u-camerino-1377-charter.note: Granted at the request of Gentile III da Varano.

u-turin-1404-founding.note: Bull of 27 October 1404; some reference works give 1405.

u-padua-1405-reform.note: Venetian rule from the early 15th century; the 1407 prohibition was not checked.

u-parma-1412-founding.note: Treccani gives 1422 for the Parma studium.

u-pavia-1412-relocation.note: Teaching was suspended 1404–1412 because of war.

u-turin-1427-relocation.note: Rashdall dates a first move to Chieri to 1421.

u-rome-1431-merger.note: The Catholic Encyclopedia suggests the Studium Curiae was suppressed in favour of the city university only under Leo X (1513–21).

u-rome-1431-reform.note: Eugenius IV reorganised the university and bought buildings at Sant'Eustachio; the wine tax was not checked.

u-genoa-1471-founding.note: Treccani dates the University of Genoa as such only from 1812.

u-pisa-1497-relocation.note: During the Pisan revolt the studio moved to Pistoia, Prato and Florence; the exact year of the move is approximate.

u-rome-1527-destruction.note: The university stayed closed for the rest of Clement VII's pontificate.

u-macerata-1540-charter.note: Bull of 1 July 1540; first degree conferred in 1541.

u-pisa-1543-refoundation.note: The botanical garden is dated 1543 by the University and 1544 by the Catholic Encyclopedia.

j-palermo-1549-founding.note: The University dates the Jesuit college to 1550.

fix.desc: Julius III grants the college the power to confer degrees in philosophy and theology; Paul IV renews it orally in 1556.

j-collegio-romano-1556-charter.note: Degree-granting power was first given by Julius III in 1552 and renewed by Paul IV.

u-turin-1560-relocation.note: The University dates the reopening at Mondovì to 1558, after closure under French occupation in 1536.

j-milan-brera-1572-founding.note: After the suppression of the Umiliati in 1571, Pius V gave the complex to the Jesuits at Borromeo's request.

u-cagliari-1606-founding.note: Royal consent to a university in Cagliari is dated 1604.

u-rome-1660-reform.note: The University dates the Biblioteca Alessandrina to 1670.

u-turin-1720-reform.note: Move to the via Po palace in 1720 under Victor Amadeus II's reform.

fix.desc: Laura Bassi receives a doctorate in philosophy and a university professorship, the first woman to hold a university chair in Europe.

u-bologna-1732-access.note: Degree in May 1732; professor of philosophy from October 1732.

t-venaria-vet-1769-founding.note: Brugnone was appointed director by letters patent of 1 September 1769.

u-malta-1769-founding.note: Decree of 22 November 1769, after a papal brief.

u-naples-1777-reform.note: The Jesuits were expelled in November 1767; the complex became a university seat in 1777.

u-malta-1800-refoundation.note: Sir Alexander Ball re-established it on 28 October 1800.

u-bologna-1803-reform.note: In 1802 Bologna and Pavia were the only public universities recognised; in 1803 the university moved to Palazzo Poggi, home of the former Academy of Sciences of the Institute.

u-palermo-1805-charter.note: Royal despatch of 3 November 1805; diploma of 12 January 1806.

fix.desc: Under French rule the university is reduced to a school of medicine dependent on the University of Pisa.

m-salerno-1811-suppression.note: Murat turned it into a Real Liceo.

u-padua-1848-suppression.note: The 8 February rising is confirmed; the closure itself was not checked.

t-turin-museo-1862-founding.note: Founded as the Museo Industriale Italiano.

t-genoa-navale-1870-founding.note: Renamed Regia Scuola d'Ingegneria Navale in 1905.

th2.note: Leading glossator; his Summae date from c. 1208–10; died between 1220 and 1232.

th3.note: Taught civil law 1213–53; died between 1259 and 1263.

th4.note: Taught at Bologna; died 1265. Start year approximate.

th6.note: Held the chair of canon law from 1302 until his death in 1348, except 1307–09 at Padua.

th7.note: Studied law at Bologna from 1320, abandoning it in 1326.

th8.note: Enrolled in canon law at about 14 and left within two years.

th10.note: Moved to Bologna in 1511 and taught there until his death in 1525.

th11.note: Lecturer at Bologna; founded its botanical garden in 1568.

th13.note: Professor from October 1732; chair of experimental physics at the Institute of Sciences from 1776; died 1778.

th14.note: Taught anatomy and obstetrics 1769–1797; dismissed in 1797 for refusing the Cisalpine oath.

th15.note: Held the chair of Italian literature 1860–1903.

th16.note: Professor in the early 14th century; tried for heresy in 1315.

th19.note: Taught from 1488 until the studium closed in the War of the League of Cambrai.

th20.note: Granted leave to study medicine in 1501; took no degree at Padua.

th21.note: Doctorate and chair in December 1537; taught until 1544. The Fabrica was printed in 1543.

th22.note: Held Vesalius's former chair of anatomy; died in Padua in 1562. Start year not checked.

th23.note: Britannica dates his succession to Falloppio's post to 1562; other accounts give 1565.

th27.note: Professor at Padua from 1700 until his death in 1714.

th28.note: Professor of medicine from 1710 and of anatomy from 1715 until his death in 1771.

th29.note: Taught law at Siena, Perugia and Naples; exact years approximate.

th32.note: His student years are uncertain: the Catholic Encyclopedia gives c. 1236, modern biographies usually 1239–1244.

th33.note: In Naples from 1272, teaching and writing, until shortly before his death in 1274.

th37.note: Professor of Italian literature from 1862 until his death in 1876.

th39.note: Worked at Salerno as translator, probably also teaching, before retiring to Monte Cassino; dates approximate.

th42.note: Taught at the Sapienza 1464–65 and again from 1473 (perhaps 1471) until his death in 1498.

th44.note: Called to the chair of medicine in 1592; died in Rome in 1603.

th45.note: Lecturer in anatomy from 1684; end date approximate.

th46.note: Called to Rome in 1871 to direct the new chemistry institute; died 1910.

th47.note: Professor at Rome from 1873 until his death in 1904.

th48.note: Taught mathematics from his ordination in 1564 until his death in 1612.

th51.note: Called in 1638 to teach mathematics, physics and oriental languages; died 1680.

th53.note: Taught law at Perugia, where Bartolus attended his lectures; exact years approximate.

th54.note: The leading medical teacher at Perugia, he died there of plague in 1348.

th55.note: Taught at Perugia from 1343 until his death in 1357.

th56.note: Taught at Perugia from about 1348 for some thirty years, with periods elsewhere.

th58.note: Taught at Pisa from 1544 and returned to Bologna in 1554.

th59.note: Prefect of the botanical garden and professor of simples from 1555, later professor of medicine.

th62.note: Offered the physics chair in 1840; died 1868.

th63.note: Entered Pisa in 1878; professor from 1883; left for Turin in 1893.

th64.note: Public readings of Dante from October 1373, broken off in early 1374.

th65.note: Taught Greek in Florence for a few years from 1397.

th69.note: Graduated in medicine at Florence in 1877; start year approximate.

th71.note: Studied at the Scuola Normale under Donato Jaja; exact years not checked.

th73.note: Taught eloquence at Pavia 1429–1431; left the city in 1433.

th75.note: Professor at Pavia from 1533, and again in 1541 and 1546.

th79.note: Appointed 1809; the chair was soon abolished.

th80.note: Graduated 1865; professor of histology from 1880 and of general pathology from 1881.

th82.note: Treccani gives a Modena professorship of logic, metaphysics and Greek, 1755–69.

th83.note: Professor from 1788, with a break after 1798 for refusing the Cisalpine oath; rector from 1814.

th84.note: In Ferrara from 1429 as tutor to Leonello d'Este; university lecturer from 29 March 1436 until his death in 1460.

th85.note: Professor of medicine at Ferrara from 1464; died there in 1524.

th87.note: Doctorate in canon law on 31 May 1503.

th88.note: Studied under Leoniceno and Manardo; the doctorate itself is undocumented.

th90.note: Chair from 1820, abolished 1822, restored to him after 1834 and held until 1850.

th92.note: Assistant from 1880, professor from 1890, until his death in 1932.

th93.note: Appointed 28 September 1755; left Turin for Berlin in 1766.

th94.note: Taught technical physics at the Museo Industriale; died 1897. Start year approximate.

th95.note: Entered the university in 1819, turned to law and graduated on 6 April 1827.

fix.role: taught mathematics and astronomy; designed and directed the Brera observatory

th96.note: Professor at Pavia from 1764 and director at Brera; removed as director in 1772 and left for Paris in 1773.

th97.note: Directed the institute from 1863 until his death in 1897.

th98.note: Taught mechanics from 1865 and directed the Politecnico from 1897 until his death in 1921.

th100.note: Appointed in 1569 at the Jesuit college that became the university; died 1575.

th103.note: Took the Palermo chair in 1780; directed the observatory from 1791.
